q: We pass some of our grid electricity to a neighbouring unit. Is that still our Scope 2?
title: Passing power to a neighbour: Scope 2
short: No. Scope 2 covers electricity you consume. Units sub-metered and billed to a neighbour or tenant are theirs to report. Keep the sub-meter readings and the recharge invoices, and subtract only what is metered, never an estimate.
audience: Factories sharing a connection with another unit

ul: A sub-meter on the neighbour's supply.
Monthly readings and the recharge bill you raise.
A note in your inventory showing the subtraction.

p: Power from your own genset or captive plant is different: all fuel burned stays in your Scope 1, and you report the exported share separately.

example.title: The subtraction
lines: Main bill: 60,000 kWh; neighbour sub-meter: 8,000 kWh
Your Scope 2: 52,000 kWh x 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) kg = 36,920 kg CO2

senseible: Senseible keeps each figure tied to its invoice, factor and method version, so a verifier can trace any number back to the document it came from.
